title: Place Value to 4,00,000
description: Master reading and writing 6-digit numbers up to 4,00,000 with Class 4 Maths. Learn Indian Number System, rounding, and comparing large numbers with solved examples and IMO practice.

topics.title: Reading and Writing 6-Digit Numbers
topics.concept:
In the Indian Number System, a 6-digit number uses places up to Lakhs. Each digit gets its value from the place it occupies.

  • Lakhs (L) = 1,00,000
  • Ten Thousands (TTh) = 10,000
  • Thousands (Th) = 1,000
  • Hundreds (H) = 100
  • Tens (T) = 10
  • Ones (O) = 1

To read a 6-digit number like 4,53,248: say the Lakhs digit first, then the Thousands group, then the last three digits. Answer: Four lakh fifty-three thousand two hundred forty-eight.

Always place commas: first comma after hundreds, second comma after thousands — e.g. 7,84,345.

examples.problem: Write 'Seven lakh eighty-four thousand three hundred fifteen' in figures.
examples.solution: Seven lakh = 7,00,000. Eighty-four thousand = 84,000. Three hundred fifteen = 315. Combine: 7,00,000 + 84,000 + 315 = 7,84,315.

examples.problem: In 5,42,789, what is the place value of the digit 4?
examples.solution: Positions from right: O(9), T(8), H(7), Th(2), TTh(4), L(5). The digit 4 is in the Ten Thousands place. Place value = 4 x 10,000 = 40,000.
9 in Lakhs = 9,00,000. 0 in Ten Thousands = 0. 6 in Thousands = 6,000. 5 in Hundreds = 500. 1 in Tens = 10. 0 in Ones = 0. Expanded form: 9,00,000 + 6,000 + 500 + 10.

recap: 6-digit numbers use the Lakhs place in the Indian Number System
Commas are placed after hundreds and then after ten-thousands: L,TTh,Th,H,T,O
Zero holds empty places — e.g. 5,08,005 has zero ten-thousands and zero hundreds
The face value is the digit itself; the place value depends on its position

topics.title: Rounding to Nearest 10,000 and Nearest Lakh
topics.concept:
Rounding makes large numbers easier to work with. We round to the nearest ten thousand or nearest lakh.

Rounding Rules:

  • Identify the place you are rounding to
  • Look at the digit immediately to its right
  • If that digit is 5 or more — Round Up (increase by 1)
  • If that digit is 4 or less — Round Down (keep same)
  • Replace all digits to the right of the target place with zeros

Memory tip: 5 or more, let it soar! 4 or less, let it rest!

examples.solution: The ten-thousands digit is 4. Look at the thousands digit: 7. Since 7 >= 5, round up. The 4 becomes 5, all digits to its right become 0. Answer: 3,50,000.
The lakhs digit is 6. Look at the ten-thousands digit: 3. Since 3 < 5, round down. The 6 stays 6, all digits to its right become 0. Answer: 6,00,000.

examples.problem: Round 8,76,543 to nearest 10,000 and nearest lakh.
examples.solution: To nearest 10,000: TTh digit is 7; next digit is 6 (>=5), round up — 8,80,000. To nearest lakh: L digit is 8; next digit is 7 (>=5), round up — 9,00,000.

recap: Rounding gives an approximate value that is easier to use
Always look one place to the RIGHT of the target place
5 or more: round up (increase target digit by 1); 4 or less: keep same
All digits to the right of the target place become zero

topics.title: Comparing Multi-Digit Numbers
topics.concept:
To compare numbers with up to 6 digits, compare digit by digit from left to right, starting with the highest place value.

Strategy:

  • Count the digits — more digits = bigger number
  • If same number of digits, compare the Lakhs place first
  • If Lakhs are equal, compare Ten Thousands, and so on
  • The first place where digits differ decides which number is greater

Use symbols: > (greater than), < (less than), = (equal to)

On a number line, numbers to the right are always greater.

examples.solution: Both 6-digit. Lakhs both 7 (same). TTh both 4 (same). Th both 5 (same). Hundreds: 6 vs 3. Since 6 > 3, the answer is 7,45,632 > 7,45,362.
Lakhs both 5 (same). Ten-thousands: 8 vs 9. Since 8 < 9, the answer is 5,89,000 < 5,98,000.

4,00,000 has largest lakhs (4). Among the three 3-lakh numbers: compare ten-thousands (4 vs 5) — 3,54,678 is largest. Between 3,45,678 and 3,45,687: compare ones (8 vs 7) — 3,45,687 > 3,45,678. Order: 3,45,678 < 3,45,687 < 3,54,678 < 4,00,000.

recap: Compare from the highest place value (Lakhs) moving right
The first place where digits differ decides the larger number
More digits always means a bigger number (e.g. 7-digit > 6-digit)
On a number line, numbers increase from left to right

questions.q: What is the place value of 8 in 8,23,456?
questions.explanation: 8 is in the Lakhs place. Place value = 8 x 1,00,000 = 8,00,000.

questions.q: Write 'Two lakh forty-five thousand six hundred seventy-eight' in figures.

questions.explanation: TTh digit is 6; next digit (Th) is 7 (>=5), round up: 4,70,000.
All have same lakhs (5). TTh: 4 vs 3 — 5,34,210 is smallest. Among 5,43,xxx: hundreds 2, 2, 0 — 5,43,210 has tens=1 > 5,43,201 (tens=0). So 5,43,210 is greatest.
Lakhs digit is 2; next digit (TTh) is 5 (>=5), round up to 3,00,000.

questions.q: In 4,56,789, which digit is in the thousands place?
questions.explanation: From left: L=4, TTh=5, Th=6, H=7, T=8, O=9. So the thousands digit is 6.

questions.q: Riya wrote the greatest 6-digit number with all different digits. What is the sum of its first and last digit?
questions.explanation: Greatest 6-digit number with all different digits = 9,87,654. First digit=9, last digit=4. Sum=9+4=13. Wait: 9,87,654 — last digit is 4. 9+4=13. Answer: 13.

questions.q: A 6-digit number rounds to 7,00,000 when rounded to the nearest lakh. Its ten-thousands digit is 5. What is the smallest such number?
questions.explanation: For a number to round up to 7,00,000, its lakhs digit must be 6 and its TTh digit must be >=5. With TTh=5, the smallest is 6,50,000.

questions.q: Using digits 2, 4, 6, 8, 0, 0 only (each used exactly once), how many different 6-digit numbers can be formed? (First digit cannot be 0)
questions.explanation: First position: 4 choices (2,4,6,8). Remaining 5 positions with digits including two 0s: 5!/2! = 60 arrangements. Total = 4 x 60 = 210.

questions.q: A number between 5,00,000 and 6,00,000 has TTh digit = its ones digit, and H digit = 3 x its ones digit. Its ones digit is 2. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Ones=2, TTh=2, H=6. Number format: 5,2?,6,2 with any Th and T. Smallest matching: 5,20,622. Best matching option: 5,22,622.

questions.q: Two numbers X and Y: X is the greatest 6-digit number with 5 in the lakhs place. Y is the smallest 6-digit number with 6 in the lakhs place. What is Y - X?
questions.explanation: X = 5,99,999 (greatest with 5 in lakhs). Y = 6,00,000 (smallest with 6 in lakhs). Y - X = 6,00,000 - 5,99,999 = 1.
